title: Control plane terraform provisioner: seamless upgrade harness and signal-driven canary rollback
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Build a Terraform module and accompanying orchestration harness to perform seamless control-plane upgrades for Redwood Private EKS clusters with signal-driven canary rollouts and automated rollback on health regressions. The harness should integrate with our provisioner, surface rich health signals, and run lightweight preflight and canary probes before committing cluster control-plane changes.

Scope:
- Terraform module extensions: upgrade plan generation, immutable canary controlplane creation, safe promotion path for controlplane replicas, and hooks for drain/rollback.
- Orchestration harness: small controller (statemachine) that sequences canary creation, traffic migration, probe evaluation, and promotion/rollback.
- Health signal collection: augment existing cluster health probes (API server latency, etcd compaction lag, kubelet ready nodes, control-plane pod restarts) and feed into evaluation engine.
- Observability: dashboard + alert rules with threshold-configurable windows and automatic incident links.
- Playbooks: runbook for manual intervention, abort criteria, and postmortem checklist.

Out of scope for this ticket: full migration of worker node upgrades, multi-region controlplane orchestration, and on-prem air-gapped packaging (follow-up tickets will address these).

Constraints & non-goals:
- Keep changes minimal in the public Terraform API so existing customers' configs do not break.
- Prioritize safety over speed: default to conservative canary sizing and longer observation windows.
- The harness must be compatible with both Hosted and Private control plane variants, but private deployment is the core focus.

Design decisions (proposed):
1) Use an immutable canary pattern: create a parallel control-plane replica in the same VPC (new EKS control plane version or config) and switch API traffic via the provisioner routing layer once probes pass.
2) Implement state machine as a lightweight Lambda + DynamoDB (or operator) prototype for iteration speed, with eventual migration to the provisioner-native reconciler.
3) Health evaluation uses weighted scoring across multiple signals; threshold breaches for X consecutive windows trigger rollback.
4) Terraform emits a plan artifact and a governance hook that the harness consumes to perform canary provisioning and promote/cleanup resources.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module supports 'canary' boolean and produces predictable resource naming for canary control-plane replicas.
- Orchestration harness can create a canary control plane, run configured probes, promote canary on pass, or rollback/cleanup on fail.
- Health signal aggregator reports to Console dashboards and exposes per-upgrade telemetry: probe pass rate, latency, errors, promotion duration, rollback reason.
- Automated rollback test in CI that injects a failing probe and validates rollback path (unit/integration).
- Documentation: PRD linked, Terraform usage examples, runbook for SREs, and a short demo video recorded.

Risks:
- Increased cost during upgrades due to parallel control-plane replicas; mitigation: default to small canary footprint and opt-in via per-customer flag.
- Race conditions in promotion path; mitigation: strict leader election and tag-based idempotency.
- API compatibility surprises; mitigation: preflight validation suite against pinned cluster versions.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha: enable for internal infra clusters only, monitor telemetry for 2 weeks.
2) Beta: opt-in for a subset of Private customers with close SRE support.
3) GA: enabled as a configurable default with conservative settings; include cost controls and time-based auto-cleanup.

Notes: ensure KMS key usage and audit logging are honored during canary operations for compliance customers.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module emits canary resources with stable naming and a 'canary' flag
